title: The Deep Extraction
premise: Elodie Fairweather has spent six years laundering her own past into a spotless life as a financial-crimes investigator, but a routine voiceprint authentication on a frozen offshore server returns a match: her own voice, recorded three years before she claims to remember anything. The server belongs to the Meridian Trust, a shell network that launders not just money but identities — and Elodie's is one of them, manufactured by the same program that trained the assassin now hunting every witness to its existence. Forced to ally with a disgraced interpol analyst and the one Meridian defector who knows how the voiceprint vault works, Elodie must smuggle the extraction ledger across three jurisdictions before a treaty-signing deadline lets Meridian legally erase its records — and everyone connected to them. In the end she trades her fabricated identity to buy the truth's release, choosing an unrecorded, found family over the clean life she built.
about_author: Emrys Galloway is the pen name of a former compliance auditor who spent a decade tracing money through jurisdictions that preferred not to be found. They write thrillers from a coastal town whose name they decline to confirm, citing ongoing litigation.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A meticulous opening of her controlled life: the packed bag behind the coats, the rehearsed cover story, a fraud case that closes too neatly. When a colleague jokes that her paperwork is 'too clean,' Elodie feels the first hairline crack in her composure. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of perpetual readiness.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Running due diligence on a frozen Meridian Trust server in Tallinn, she submits a standard voice authentication — and the system greets her by an unfamiliar name, with credentials created three years before her earliest memory. She terminates the session and lies to her supervisor about what happened. Beat: vertigo; the floor of her identity gives way.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches Airports
chapters.summary: Assassin Corvin Asche's POV, cold and procedural. He receives a kill list keyed to the Meridian voiceprint vault and recognizes one name as already flagged for 'special handling.' He flies to London, observing rather than striking, establishing the pattern of patience that defines him. Beat: dread established through calm.

chapters.title: What the Bag Is For
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She runs her own records through private databases and finds gaps — hospital admissions, bank accounts, a marriage certificate she cannot recall. Her mentor, Ivo Brandt, notices her digging and warns her off with genuine fear. That night someone searches her flat without taking anything. Beat: paranoia becomes evidence.

chapters.title: The Defector in Rotterdam
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Nadia Okafor, a suspended interpol analyst who has chased Meridian for years and was discredited for it. She contacts Elodie through a dead-drop message only a Meridian-trained asset would understand. Their first meeting is a test neither fully passes. Beat: wary recognition between two people who trust nothing.

chapters.title: Ledger of Selves
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. She shows Elodie the pattern: Meridian doesn't launder money so much as people — building complete false histories for operatives, then holding those histories hostage. Elodie's file exists; its extraction would prove everything. But touching the vault trips a silent alarm. Beat: hope arriving with a price tag.

chapters.title: Ivo Knows
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Confronting Ivo, she learns he was her handler — that her 'recruitment' into financial crimes was Meridian placing an asset inside the investigative world, and that he has been protecting her from activation ever since. He refuses to help further and burns his own notes. Beat: betrayal braided with love.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. He eliminates a Meridian archivist in Lisbon who tried to sell fragments of the ledger, recovering a partial index — enough to know Elodie's file is the master key. He reports to a handler whose voice he has never heard. Beat: the hunt tightens; the reader sees the clock start.

chapters.title: Run Clean
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. With Ivo's warning call seconds ahead of a raid team, Elodie grabs the go-bag and vanishes using tradecraft she didn't know she had — muscle memory betraying training she can't remember. The chapter ends with her realizing her body remembers being an operative. Beat: terror fused with grim competence.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Server
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. From a safehouse she maps the political trap: British, Estonian, and American agencies each hold partial jurisdiction over the Tallinn server, and Meridian's lawyers will legally purge it at the upcoming financial-treaty signing in eleven days. Extraction must happen before, or never. Beat: the ticking clock made concrete.

chapters.title: The Third Chair
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The team gains its final member: Tomas Reyes, a nervous Meridian systems engineer who built the voiceprint vault and wants out. His price is protection; his liability is enormous. Elodie must decide whether to trust the man whose code holds her past hostage. Beat: fragile alliance, found family's first stitch.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Personal Edition
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Using the partial index, Corvin reconstructs Elodie's original identity — and finds it deliberately corrupted by someone inside Meridian years ago. Someone wanted her unreadable. He begins to wonder who his real target is. Beat: the hunter's certainty cracks.

chapters.title: Amsterdam Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A meet with a Meridian insider goes wrong; the insider dies delivering half a passphrase, and Elodie escapes only because her forgotten training takes over — she disarms an attacker with movements that horrify her. Nadia sees it and says nothing. Beat: the cost of survival written on her own hands.

chapters.title: What Ivo Buried
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ivo, dying of the illness he hid, leaves Elodie a letter and a physical key: proof he corrupted her file himself to keep Meridian from reactivating her. The letter ends mid-sentence, interrupted by Corvin, who needs Ivo alive just long enough to talk. Beat: grief and guilt compounding.

chapters.title: The Interrogation Room That Isn't
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin questions Ivo in a Meridian black site and hears, for the first time, that the organization's true product is deniable people — and that Corvin himself may be file zero. He kills Ivo swiftly, almost mercifully, and lies in his report. Beat: the assassin turns unreliable to his own masters.

chapters.title: Eleven Hours to Tallinn
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Reeling from Ivo's death, the team executes the infiltration plan: Reyes will walk in as a maintenance contractor while Elodie's voiceprint opens the vault from inside. Nadia handles the diplomatic chess, feeding each government just enough to freeze Meridian's purge order. Beat: resolve forged from loss.

chapters.title: Inside the Vault
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The vault opens to her voice like a door to her own skull. She finds her file — and thousands like it, including children's intake records. Downloading everything triggers the alarm she knew was coming. Corvin appears in the corridor, weapon raised, and does not fire. Beat: moral horror and suspended violence.

chapters.title: Assassin's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Cornered between his orders and the files proving he was Meridian's first fabrication, Corvin makes his move: he kills the site security chief covering the purge and hands Elodie the exit route, asking nothing except that his name be in the record. Beat: redemption priced in treason.

chapters.title: The Treaty Floor
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Climax part one: at the treaty signing, Nadia detonates the scandal publicly, distributing the ledger to delegates and press simultaneously so no single government can bury it. Meridian's lawyers scramble; the purge order collapses under daylight. Beat: catharsis through procedure — the bureaucrat's weapon fired perfectly.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Climax part two: Meridian's director corners Elodie with an offer — her original identity restored, her old life returned, if she surrenders the ledger. She refuses, understanding at last that the self she built these six years is the real one. Corvin sacrifices himself covering their escape. Beat: identity chosen, not recovered.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks later: governments squabble over Meridian's ruins, Reyes testifies from hiding, and Nadia is reinstated. Elodie's official file is sealed — she is, technically, no one. She unpacks the go-bag at last, keeping it packed out of habit, then out of choice. Beat: quiet grief turning toward peace.

chapters.title: The Deep Extraction
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, epilogue. On Nadia's houseboat — the found family gathered, imperfect and alive — Elodie records a new voiceprint, this time for a safe belonging to all of them. The final line reveals she kept one page of her file: not her past, but Ivo's note in the margin: 'She chose well.' Beat: survival's price paid, and worth it.
